skill.name: file-organizer
skill.description: Analyzes directories, identifies duplicates, proposes structures, and moves or renames files after user approval.
skill.summary: Organize cluttered directories with reviewed plans, duplicate checks, and logged file changes.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: All 12 static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown fences or benign prose; no Ruby backtick execution or reconnaissance appears. The skill nevertheless presents shell commands that accept unquoted directory placeholders and a plain `mv` example that may overwrite files. These operational risks require safer command construction and collision handling before unattended use.

remediation.issue: Unquoted directory placeholders in shell commands
remediation.suggestion: Pass paths as structured arguments when possible. Otherwise, validate and shell-quote every user-selected path before execution.

remediation.issue: File moves can overwrite existing destinations
remediation.suggestion: Check destination collisions first, use non-overwriting move options, and record a reversible manifest for every change.

semantic_findings.title: Shell Injection Through Unquoted Path Placeholders
semantic_findings.description: Commands interpolate the user-selected `[target_directory]` or `[directory]` placeholder without shell quoting. A path containing shell metacharacters could execute unintended commands if substituted directly.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples visibly place path placeholders into shell command positions without quoting. Runtime substitution is agent-dependent, so exploitation is plausible but not guaranteed.

semantic_findings.title: Potential Overwrite During File Moves
semantic_findings.description: The example uses plain `mv`, which can replace an existing destination without warning. This conflicts with the later instruction to handle filename conflicts gracefully.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented command uses `mv` without a no-clobber or interactive option. An existing writable destination can therefore be overwritten before the prose safeguard is applied.

content.value_statement: Cluttered directories hide important files and waste storage. This skill reviews contents, proposes a structure, and applies approved moves, renames, or duplicate cleanup.
actual_capabilities: Reviews file types, sizes, dates, and directory structure with standard shell tools.
Groups files by type, purpose, project, or date.
Guides duplicate checks using file hashes, filenames, and sizes.
Produces an organization plan before changing files.
Creates folders and performs approved file moves or renames.
Summarizes completed changes and suggests maintenance routines.
limitations: Requires access to the target directories and local shell tools.
Uses platform-dependent commands, including `md5` and GNU-style `find` options.
Does not provide an automated rollback mechanism.
Needs user review before deleting files or resolving ambiguous duplicates.

use_cases.title: Clean a Downloads Folder
use_cases.description: Sort mixed downloads into clear categories while identifying large, old, and duplicate candidates.

use_cases.title: Consolidate Project Archives
use_cases.description: Separate active projects from completed work and standardize folder and file names.

use_cases.title: Prepare Shared Records
use_cases.description: Review team files, propose a consistent structure, and flag ambiguous items before migration.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Folder
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [directory] without changing files. Summarize file types, large items, date ranges, and the main organization problems.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Cleanup
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [directory] and propose a conservative folder structure. List every planned move, rename, archive, and duplicate decision for approval.
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a reviewable plan before changes.

prompt_templates.title: Organize Approved Files
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the approved plan to [directory]. Avoid overwrites, log every change, preserve timestamps, and stop when any destination is ambiguous.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Archive Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [directories], identify duplicate candidates, design active and archive structures, and produce a reversible migration plan with collision checks.

output_examples.input: Review my Downloads folder without changing anything.
output: Current state: 286 files across 14 types, with installers and screenshots forming the largest groups.
Suggested folders: Documents, Images, Installers, Archives, and To-Sort.
Review needed: 12 duplicate candidates and 9 files older than one year.

output_examples.input: Prepare a conservative cleanup plan for my completed client projects.
output: Archive 18 completed project folders by client and year.
Keep four active projects in their current locations.
Confirm three naming conflicts and two duplicate groups before any changes.

best_practices: Start with read-only analysis and define directories that must remain untouched.
Review the complete move, rename, archive, and deletion plan before approval.
Use collision checks and a reversible change log for every operation.
anti_patterns: Do not organize an entire home directory without a clearly approved scope.
Do not delete duplicate candidates based only on similar names or sizes.
Do not substitute raw user input into shell commands or overwrite existing destinations.

faq.question: Does this skill delete files automatically?
faq.answer: No. It instructs the agent to request confirmation before deletion, but users should still review every proposed removal.

faq.question: Can it organize an entire home directory?
faq.answer: It can analyze broad scopes, but smaller directories reduce mistakes and make approval easier.

faq.question: How does it identify duplicates?
faq.answer: It suggests checks based on hashes, filenames, and sizes. Hash tooling and command behavior vary by operating system.

faq.question: Can I undo changes?
faq.answer: The skill recommends logging moves, but it does not provide an automated rollback tool. Keep backups and require a reversible manifest.

faq.question: Which operating systems are supported?
faq.answer: The examples use Unix shell commands. Some commands require adaptation between macOS, Linux, and other environments.

faq.question: Will it preserve file dates?
faq.answer: The instructions require preserving modification dates, but actual behavior depends on the selected command and filesystem.
